A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey. Their readable text, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching content moved into the later appendices.

before.justification: v1 synthesizes published research and proposes conceptual taxonomies. Its empirical findings and dataset statistics are attributed to other works; no original empirical analysis is reported.

after.justification: Appendix F/Table 5 supplies a small original qualitative data-analysis output: politeness-related annotations of a five-turn Reddit discussion. Its caption identifies a forthcoming toolkit used to produce the annotations. This is an illustrative analysis, without quantitative evaluation.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an executable facilitation algorithm or model architecture. The revised taxonomies and Table 4 summarize concepts and possible applications; the toolkit mention does not document a new algorithm or changed model.

E1.justification: v2 newly uses a five-turn Reddit Change My View discussion for the annotation example in Appendix F/Table 5. v1 only surveys these resources. Removing Webis-WikiDebate-18 from Table 1 changes the literature catalogue, not an evaluated benchmark suite.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against a proposed system. Table 4 contrasts pre-LLM and LLM approaches conceptually, without conducting a baseline comparison.

E3.justification: The new Table 5 example introduces a limited annotation procedure covering hedging, first- and second-person references, direct questions, and positive and negative sentiment in the displayed turns. No benchmark settings are revised. The literature-search criteria are retained when moved from v1 Section 4 to v2 Appendix D.

E4.justification: Appendix F/Table 5 adds a worked discussion case illustrating how politeness-related linguistic cues coexist and could inform facilitator responses. v1 has no corresponding case illustration. No ablation, robustness test, or measured intervention outcome is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests for its own analysis. v2's discussion of LLM nondeterminism and annotation reliability summarizes cited research rather than introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds concrete annotation outputs, including marking 'could' as hedging and 'worse than useless' as negative sentiment. Literature-result summaries also change: v2 Section 6.3 specifies Cho et al.'s limitations concerning cooperation and mutual respect, while omitting v1's detailed Shahid et al. constructiveness findings. Retained Table 1 dataset sizes are unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version contains formal mathematical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations. Changes to terminology and conceptual taxonomies do not introduce formal mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The central interdisciplinary survey, discussion-quality taxonomy, and LLM roadmap contributions remain. The dataset-taxonomy contribution is narrowed from three categories to two by dropping User Tactics, and the conclusion newly qualifies discussion-quality categories as flexible.

C2.justification: v2 substantially connects quality dimensions to specific facilitation actions in Section 4/Table 4, distinguishes facilitation from content moderation, and explains overlapping taxonomy categories. Sections 6.2–6.3 and 11 add substantive qualifications about cost, unreliable annotations, nondeterminism, bias, consent, and human oversight. Conversely, the roadmap removes v1's explicit meta-evaluation agenda and requirement to establish synthetic discussions as reliable human-behavior proxies.

D1.justification: Table 5 newly identifies its annotation mechanism as a soon-to-be-released discussion-evaluation toolkit. This adds limited implementation provenance and availability information, but supplies no toolkit name, version, access link, or reproducible configuration. Existing search criteria and keywords are retained.

R1.justification: The literature synthesis expands substantially around pragmatic evaluation, prosocial facilitation, and limitations of LLM social simulation. Additions include Grice, Lambert et al., Bisbee et al., Rossi et al., Atil et al., and Neumann et al. Some earlier coherence and argumentation references are removed, and the positioning more explicitly emphasizes connecting evaluation to facilitation.

P1.justification: The introduction, discussion-quality coverage, and roadmap are extensively rewritten. LLM evaluation observations are consolidated into new Section 4.5, methodology moves to Appendix D, and an ethical-considerations section plus Appendices E–F are added. The author and affiliation block also changes.

P2.justification: v1's taxonomy tree is replaced by an expanded appendix representation in Table 4, while v2 Figure 1 becomes a new conceptual overview. Table 5 adds a color-coded discussion example. Table 1 is compacted and its category structure changes; Figure 2 retains its graphic with a revised caption.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the survey's practical clarity by distinguishing moderation from facilitation and connecting quality dimensions to intervention choices. Its expanded treatment of reliability, bias, and oversight also makes the recommendations better qualified. These gains support a limited net improvement, tempered by the loss of the explicit meta-evaluation and synthetic-proxy validation agenda from v1's roadmap.
